Do NOT modify any files. Read the relevant code carefully (use rg/grep and Read). Your job is to produce an accurate, concrete implementation plan that another engineer can apply directly without re-reading much.

- List every repo-relative file path that needs editing.
- Quote the EXACT current code (with file:line) at each site that must change.
- Give the exact replacement code where it is under ~40 lines.
- Note related call sites / type declarations that must change in sync.
- If tests exist under test/ut/spec that relate, name them.

Be precise and complete. Accuracy matters more than brevity, but do not dump whole files - quote only the relevant regions.

=== requirements/axislabel-formatter-indexing.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.

  '
=== requirements/axislabel-formatter-index.yaml
title: 'feat(axis): axisLabel `formatter` can receive its index for working with `customValues`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Axis label callbacks can format the label value, but authors working with `customValues` also need to know which generated tick they are formatting in order to line up external labels correctly.

  ## Desired outcome

  `axisLabel.formatter` should receive the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic can work reliably with `customValues`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick and can build labels from that position information.

  '

  ## Acceptance signals

  A time axis that uses both `axisLabel.customValues` and `axisLabel.formatter` renders normally and passes the formatter the expected label values.

input.risks:
1. TYPE INFERENCE: zrender's `map` declares the callback index as optional (`index?: number`, node_modules/zrender/src/core/util.ts:335-339), so the inferred type of `index` is `number | undefined`. That is fine because `makeLabelFormatter` returns `(tick: ScaleTick, idx?: number) => string`. Do not add an explicit `index: number` annotation — under strictFunctionTypes that can fail to type-check. The existing `makeRealNumberLabels` does exactly this (unannotated `function (tick, idx)`), so follow it.

2. TIME AXIS SEMANTICS: `tickValuesToNumbers` (src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:111-121) prepends/appends a duplicate of the first/last value for time axes ("The first and last tick/label don't get drawn"). After the fix those two duplicates occupy their own indices (0 and 1; n-2 and n-1), which is the intended "index of the rendered item in the filtered label list". If a reviewer expects the drawn labels to start at index 0, that expectation is wrong for time axes — the offset is pre-existing and upstream keeps the filtered-list index. Also note `nums.sort()` on line 116 is a lexicographic sort of numbers (pre-existing bug); do not fix it here, it would change which values survive the extent filter.

3. ADJACENT UNFIXED BUG (separate requirement, do not fold in unless the test forces it): a time axis using `axisLabel.customValues` together with a *function* formatter currently throws, because custom ticks are created as `{value: numval}` with no `time`, and src/util/time.ts:345-346 does `time: tick.time, level: tick.time.level` inside `leveledFormat`. That is requirements/time-axis-customvalues-formatter.yaml, not this one. If a verification test for this requirement uses a time axis with a function formatter, it will crash before it can observe the index; the minimal guard would be `level: tick.time && tick.time.level` at src/util/time.ts:346 — flag it, but keep it out of this change unless required.

4. CATEGORY AXES: on a category axis a function formatter ignores the passed index by design (src/coord/axisHelper.ts:259-271 substitutes `tick.value - axis.scale.getExtent()[0]` for back compat). So a test asserting sequential indices must use a value/log/time axis, not `type: 'category'`. Do not "fix" the category branch — that would be a breaking change explicitly documented in the comment there.

5. STRING FORMATTERS are unaffected (index unused), so no snapshot/visual regression is expected for the common `formatter: '{value}'` case; the only behavior delta is the second argument handed to function formatters on custom-value labels (previously `undefined`).
